classification.difficultyReason: Constructs rhombus diagonals and establishes two parallel relationships before using perpendicular diagonals.

content.prompt: $ABCD$ is a straight line such that $AB=BC=CD$ and $BCPQ$ is a rhombus. The lines produced through $AQ$ and $DP$ meet at $R$. Prove that $\angle ARD$ is a right angle.

spec.description: Triangle ARD enclosing rhombus BCPQ; equal-segment double ticks retained. Ordinary source blue becomes black.
spec.mathematics: A,B,C,D collinear in order; AB=BC=CD=BQ=QP=PC; Q on AR and P on RD.
spec.answerVisibility: Givens only; auxiliary diagonals are introduced in the solution.

answer.short:
$\angle ARD=90^\circ$.

The rhombus diagonals are respectively parallel to $AR$ and $DR$, and are perpendicular.
answer.worked:
Draw the diagonals $BP$ and $CQ$ of the rhombus.

Since $AB=BQ$, $\angle AQB=\angle QAB$. The exterior-angle theorem in $\triangle ABQ$ gives $\angle QBC=2\angle QAB$.

The diagonal $BP$ bisects $\angle QBC$, so $\angle PBC=\angle QAB$. Hence $BP\parallel AQ$ by equal corresponding angles.

Similarly, $CP=CD$ gives $\angle CPD=\angle PDC$, and $\angle BCP=2\angle PDC$. Since $CQ$ bisects $\angle BCP$, $\angle BCQ=\angle PDC$, so $CQ\parallel DP$.

The diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular, so $BP\perp CQ$. Therefore $AR\perp DR$ and $\angle ARD=90^\circ$.
